newsitem.title: ITALY: FREE PHONE CALLS WITH ADS REACH ITALY.
newsitem.headline: FREE PHONE CALLS WITH ADS REACH ITALY.

text.p: Italians, phone lovers who face some of the highest call charges in Europe, are being given the chance to use the telephone for free -- provided they don't mind commercials cutting into their conversation.
Corriere della Sera newspaper reported on Wednesday that the Promotion System Phone (PSP) service was carrying out a trial in three northern Italian towns.
A similar service was launched in Sweden last year by a telephone advertising company called Gratistelefon -- or Free Telephone.
Gratistelefon said in January people were making 30,000 free phone calls a day, with each call being interrupted by a 10-second ad after the first minute and then once every three minutes.
In Italy, Corriere della Sera said the new PSP service was being launched by a Tuscan entrepreneur, Paolo Balestri.
"We're amazed with the success. People didn't know what to make of it at first but then word got around and now we're inundated with requests," it quoted Balestri as saying.
"We seem to be getting enough advertising, too. We'll soon be able to cover our costs."
PSP users hear three ads, lasting three to five seconds each, before their call is put through. Their conversation is then interrupted every 100 seconds by another spot ad.
In return, they are allowed 15 minutes of free phone time for local calls -- the line cuts off after that time -- and a 30-percent discount on the cost of phoning other cities.
"I was a bit sceptical at first," Carmen Bonatti, a pensioner, told the newspaper. "But my doubts disappeared when I got the bill."
The newspaper said the trial was due to be extended soon to more than 60 cities, including Milan, Rome and Florence.
No comment was immediately available from Balestri's company, Primosat.
